name: Lauren R Hobart
current_role: President & CEO, DICK'S Sporting Goods (incl. Foot Locker); independent director, Marriott International
profile: Penn and Stanford MBA graduate who worked at Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase and 14 years at PepsiCo (incl. CMO of carbonated soft drinks NA) before joining DICK'S as CMO in 2011. Became president in 2017 and in Feb 2021 succeeded Ed Stack as CEO, the first non-Stack-family CEO; she now also runs the acquired Foot Locker business.
interesting_fact: She is only the third CEO in DICK'S 75+-year history and the first from outside the founding Stack family.
deep_cut_fact: She personally initiated DICK'S 'Sports Matter' program in 2014, which funds grants, equipment and sponsorships for underserved youth sports teams; she is also president of The DICK'S Sporting Goods Foundation.
notes: Fortune (Mar 2022) profiled how her psychology interest shaped her leadership - useful hook. Best route is DICK'S corporate communications.

name: Anutthara Bharadwaj
current_role: Partner, ICONIQ (per TechCrunch/Toast bios); board director, Toast Inc.; former President of Atlassian (2023-Dec 2025)
profile: Known as Anu Bharadwaj; RV College of Engineering grad who spent ~11 years at Microsoft (Visual Studio ALM/TFS) before joining Atlassian in 2014 as head of product for Jira. Rose to COO (2021) and President (2023), then left Atlassian on 31 Dec 2025 after 12 years; joined Toast's board in Oct 2025 and is now listed as a partner at ICONIQ.
interesting_fact: In 2016 she took a year-long sabbatical for wildlife conservation fieldwork: rescuing lions from canned hunting in South Africa, GPS-collaring cheetahs in Namibia, monitoring penguin rookeries in Antarctica.
deep_cut_fact: Her first job at Microsoft was as a developer building 'Terrarium', a game; she said: 'As a gamer and a nerd, I couldn't believe they actually paid me for this job!'
notes: Departure from Atlassian announced Aug 2025, effective 31 Dec 2025. ICONIQ affiliation comes from TechCrunch contributor page and Toast bio; one site lists Operator Collective instead - confirm. Chaired Atlassian Foundation. Best route likely via ICONIQ or Toast board.

name: Patrick Arthur Kelly
current_role: Co-President & Chief Operating Officer, Cipher Digital Inc. (formerly Cipher Mining; Nasdaq: CIFR)
profile: Co-founder and former COO of Stone Ridge Asset Management (operations, technology, accounting) who became COO of Cipher Mining at its 2021 formation and Co-President in 2023. He helps run Cipher's Texas data center portfolio as it pivots from bitcoin mining to leasing HPC/AI capacity to hyperscalers, now as Cipher Digital.
interesting_fact: Cipher extended its Barber Lake (Texas) data center lease with a hyperscale tenant to 20 years, lifting contracted revenue to over $9 billion - a flagship bitcoin-miner-to-AI-infrastructure pivot.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto/data centers he was a co-founder of Stone Ridge Asset Management, the alternative-investment firm, where he served as COO overseeing operations, technology and accounting.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast (ERCOT, bitcoin-to-AI pivot). Low public profile; route via Dukas Linden PR. Aggregators say DePaul finance grad and CFA charterholder - unverified.

name: George A Scangos
current_role: Director, Vir Biotechnology (founding CEO 2017-2023) and director, Agilent Technologies
profile: Biotech veteran from Lynn, Massachusetts: Johns Hopkins biology professor, then Bayer Biotechnology, CEO of Exelixis (1996-2010, took it public), CEO of Biogen (2010-2016, refocused it on neurology), and founding CEO of Vir Biotechnology (2017-2023). Retired as Vir CEO in April 2023 but remains on Vir's and Agilent's boards.
interesting_fact: He chaired PhRMA in 2016 and later led the Biotechnology Innovation Organization's industry response to COVID-19 while Vir developed COVID antibodies.
deep_cut_fact: As a Yale postdoc with geneticist Frank Ruddle he helped create the first transgenic mouse; before grad school he briefly worked as an MIT lab technician and as a sales rep for a lab-supply company.

public_contacts.value: kpatel@vir.bio (Kiki Patel, Head of IR, Vir)

notes: Retired from operating roles; now a board member only. Gave a Stanford eCorner talk 'Making a difference in biotech' (stvp.stanford.edu) - good prep material. Biotech, not energy, so podcast fit is the entrepreneurship angle.

name: Stephan B. Tanda
current_role: Advisor to AptarGroup through end-2026 (President & CEO 2017-Aug 2026; retiring from Aptar board by end of 2026); director, Ingredion
profile: Austrian-born engineer and executive who served on Royal DSM's managing board (running its ~$5.5B nutrition business and pharma JVs) before becoming CEO of AptarGroup, the Crystal Lake, IL maker of drug-delivery and dispensing systems, in Feb 2017. Gael Touya succeeded him as CEO on 1 Sep 2026; Tanda is advising through year-end.
interesting_fact: Under his tenure Aptar was repeatedly named by TIME as one of the World's Most Sustainable Companies (three consecutive years by 2026).
deep_cut_fact: He is a trained plastics engineer - his first degree is in plastics engineering from the Montanuniversität Leoben in Austria - before a Wharton MBA; fitting for someone who went on to run a company built on polymer dispensing pumps and closures.
notes: CEO succession announced 17 Mar 2026 (https://aptar.com/news-events/aptar-announces-gael-touya-as-its-next-chief-executive-officer-stephan-b-tanda-to-retire-by-the-end-of-the-year). Will be fully retired from Aptar by 2027, so Aptar comms may be a weakening route; Ingredion board remains. DSM background: https://shawlocal.com/2017/02/23/new-leader-takes-over-at-crystal-lake-based-aptar/a81bm2q

name: Fabrizio Freda
current_role: Independent director, BlackRock (since 2012; re-elected 2026); former President & CEO, The Estée Lauder Companies (2009-Dec 2024)
profile: Naples-born executive (University of Naples Federico II, 1981) who spent ~25 years at Procter & Gamble, ending as president of Global Snacks, before joining Estée Lauder as COO in 2008 and CEO in 2009. He led the beauty group's long global/China expansion, retired as CEO at end-2024, advised the company into fiscal 2026, and sits on BlackRock's board.
interesting_fact: In 2015 Italy's President Sergio Mattarella awarded him the Order of Merit for Labour (Cavaliere del Lavoro), one of Italy's top honours for business leaders.
deep_cut_fact: Mid-way through his P&G career he took a two-year detour to Gucci as international director of marketing and strategic planning, returning to P&G after Gucci's 1988 sale to an investor group.
notes: Retired from operating roles; BlackRock board contact is formal (routes via corporate secretary). A 2018 iItaly/Casa Italiana NYU interview ('Inventing the Unexpected for the Selfie Generation') discusses Naples creativity - good prep.

name: Bernardo Hees
current_role: Operating Partner, The Cranemere Group (New York); director of Avis Budget Group, Krispy Kreme and Bunge Global
profile: Brazilian executive and former 3G Capital partner who ran railroad operator America Latina Logistica, then Burger King (2010-13), H.J. Heinz (2013) and Kraft Heinz (2015-19) under 3G/Berkshire ownership. Later chaired and then served as executive chairman of Avis Budget (2020-24); since 2024 an operating partner at Cranemere and a board member at Avis, Krispy Kreme and Bunge.
interesting_fact: When he joined Avis Budget as chairman in Feb 2020 he committed $15 million of his own money to buy Avis shares to align with shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: He began at America Latina Logistica in 1998 as a logistics analyst after earlier bank jobs and an MBA, and rose to become CEO of what became Latin America's largest railroad/logistics company.
notes: Cranemere team page lists him as Operating Partner, New York. Railroad/logistics and food CPG background; no personal public channels found.

name: Andrew Stewart Plump
current_role: Director and President, Research & Development, Takeda Pharmaceutical
profile: Physician-scientist (MIT BS, Rockefeller PhD, UCSF MD) who led cardiovascular research at Merck and was deputy to the R&D president at Sanofi before joining Takeda in 2015 to run global R&D. He drove Takeda's R&D restructuring toward focused therapeutic areas, partnerships and data/digital-driven drug discovery, and sits on Takeda's board.
interesting_fact: He orchestrated a multi-year transformation of Takeda R&D after 2015, streamlining its global footprint and building a partnership-heavy, multi-modality pipeline.
deep_cut_fact: As a Rockefeller PhD student with Jan Breslow he was first author of the 1992 Cell paper creating the apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE knockout) mouse, which became one of the most widely used animal models of atherosclerosis.
notes: Goes by Andy. Boston-based. LinkedIn is linked from his official Takeda bio. Status confirmed from Takeda leadership page (Nov 2026).

name: Keith Rabois
current_role: Managing Director, Khosla Ventures; Chairman of Opendoor (since Sept 2025)
profile: PayPal Mafia operator-investor (PayPal EVP, LinkedIn VP, Square COO) turned VC at Khosla Ventures and Founders Fund, with early bets on DoorDash, Affirm, Faire, Stripe, Ramp, Airbnb and Palantir. He co-founded home-buying platform Opendoor in 2014, returned to Khosla as managing director in 2024, and was named Opendoor chairman in Sept 2025 alongside new CEO Kaz Nejatian.
interesting_fact: Consistently on the Forbes Midas List (as high as #4 in the U.S.); at Khosla he led the first institutional investments in DoorDash, Affirm and Faire.
deep_cut_fact: His official Khosla Ventures bio boasts '4700+ Barry's Bootcamp classes completed' - a fitness streak he lists alongside his 15+ IPO-bound investments.
notes: Very active on X (@rabois) - most direct public channel. Miami-based since 2020. Outspoken political posts have drawn controversy (incl. Jan 2026, disavowed by Khosla colleagues) - be aware. Opendoor chairman role per CNBC 10 Sep 2025 headline cited on Wikipedia.

His current activities could not be established.

name: Samir Bodas
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO, Icertis (current role unconfirmed; Icertis now led by interim co-CEOs, Jim Moffatt chairs the board)
profile: Former CEO of Indian IT-services firm Aztecsoft who co-founded Icertis in 2009 (Pune roots, Bellevue, WA HQ) and built it into a leading AI-powered contract lifecycle management platform valued around $5B. Anand Subbaraman joined in 2024 and later led the company; in July 2026 Icertis appointed interim co-CEOs and a new board chair.
interesting_fact: Icertis grew from a Pune-based startup into a top-ranked enterprise contract-intelligence vendor whose customers include Microsoft and Accenture; its board's lead independent director is Penny Pritzker.
deep_cut_fact: Before Icertis he was CEO of Aztecsoft, an Indian software-services company.
notes: Exact timing of Bodas's handover to Subbaraman not verified (Icertis July 2026 release only says Subbaraman 'joined Icertis in 2024'). Bodas's current activity not verified because web-search quota ran out; no sign of death found. Icertis comms may no longer be the right route.

name: Daniel Kirchert
current_role: Former co-founder, president and CEO of Byton (current role not verified)
profile: German automotive executive who co-founded China-based electric-vehicle startup Byton with Carsten Breitfeld, first as president and, from April 2019, as CEO. He left in October 2020 amid Byton's financial troubles; the company later stalled after a planned Foxconn partnership and is now defunct.
interesting_fact: Byton, headquartered in Nanjing and incorporated in Hong Kong (2016-17), unveiled the all-electric M-Byte SUV concept and in Jan 2021 struck a strategic partnership with Foxconn, which planned to invest US$200M before putting the project on hold.
notes: Byton is defunct (bankrupt), so any Hurun-based wealth figure is likely stale. Pre-Byton career (reportedly senior roles at BMW Brilliance and Infiniti China) and post-2020 activities not verified - web-search quota ran out mid-lane. No sign of death found. Needs follow-up.

name: Sanket Hattimattur
current_role: Non-Executive Director, Brainbees Solutions Ltd (FirstCry) since 1 Apr 2025
profile: Early FirstCry team member who joined on 9 Sept 2010, weeks before the Pune-based baby/kids e-commerce site launched, and served as Executive Director and Chief of Staff overseeing India strategy, M&A and international expansion. FirstCry listed on India's NSE/BSE in Aug 2024; he moved to a non-executive board role in April 2025.
interesting_fact: He has been with FirstCry since before its November 2010 launch and helped steer it through its August 2024 stock-market IPO (raising about INR 4,194 crore).
deep_cut_fact: Before FirstCry he worked at Brainvisa Technologies (where FirstCry founder Supam Maheshwari was previously president), Deutsche Bank's Global Markets Centre and Tata AIG Life; his degree is a B.Com in financial accounting and auditing from the University of Mumbai.
notes: Low public profile. Listed as a sitting director on FirstCry's IR site (Nov 2026).
